_metadata.description: Iterative editing over existing audio: separation, cover, repaint, accompaniment.

requirements.title: Stem separation independent of the generator
requirements.description: Stem separation is served by a dedicated separator that does not require the composition model to be resident, because the generation variant that fits constrained VRAM may not expose separation at all.

validation.notes: The independent Music Tools analysis/separation job path exists. A live owner-backed separation receipt and consumer verification remain unproven.

requirements.title: Section repaint and cover preserve identity
requirements.description: Repaint regenerates a bounded time range while leaving the remainder byte-identical, and cover restyles a track while preserving its structure — so a near-miss can be edited rather than rerolled.

validation.notes: No section repaint or structure-preserving cover operation is exposed by Music Tools. Do not mark implemented until an owner job emits exact input/output hashes, bounded edit ranges, and an immutable operation receipt.

requirements.title: Remix and sample jobs emit immutable lineage receipts
requirements.description: A successful remix or sample-based arrangement is a durable Music Tools job whose owner-issued receipt binds every source SHA-256 and excerpt range to the derived output SHA-256, operation kind, tool/model revision, license lane, and non-widening rights scope. Consumers verify receipts by job identity instead of trusting draft metadata or a generic result reference.

validation.notes: Durable-job receipt validation round-trips owner evidence and rejects failed jobs, identity/hash/range mismatches and invalid rights scope.
Request, managed-source boundary, excerpt duration parsing and deterministic remix/sample filter contracts are covered. The worker is registered before persisted-job recovery.
Pending an authorized bounded run: listener must hear actual derived files and match their audio hashes and lineage receipt to the originating release packet.
